newsitem.title: UK: HK stocks in London up on HSBC but seen vulnerable.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks in London up on HSBC but seen vulnerable.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks in London rose on Friday on the back of strength in heavyweight banking group HSBC Holdings, but traders said prices were vulnerable on Monday in the first full week since Britain handed the colony over to China.
Early strength in the FTSE 100 also helped stocks up from their lows registered in weaker Hong Kong trading.
U.S. markets were closed on Friday for their Independence Day holiday, however, sapping liquidity.
HSBC climbed HK$2 to HK$243 after hitting a record high of HK$244.625.
The leading Hang Seng London Reference Index .HSLR gained 39.51 points to 14,862.48.
"The market looks like it should come back a bit further, led by the property stocks," said one trader.
Euphoria surrounding the handover to China, which pushed shares sharply higher last week, may be cooling off, traders said.
Stocks in Hong Kong tumbled to a sharply lower close as uncertainty about government plans to curb real estate prices rattled property shares, traders said.
-- John Hanley, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4366 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
